utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva, you are to continue with your examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning to you and to Your Honours

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Good morning, 116. I think I have about 40 minutes left, so we are going to try to be as quick as possible this morning. We finished yesterday with your sketch that you produced regarding the incident in Hrasnica on the 7th of April, 1995, and now I want to show you another document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, just for your information, this exhibit or this 65 ter document that I'm going to show the witness, I indicated to the Defence just over 24 hours prior to the witness' testimony, so, in other words, it wasn't within the 48 hours, but I have discussed this with counsel and I understand that she was no objection to me using this document. Just for your information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very good.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Could I have 65 ter 787E brought up on the screen, please, and if it could not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, while that is being brought up, after your investigation in Hrasnica, did you produce a forensic report on your on-site investigation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I made a report on the criminal investigation of the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: On the screen now, on the right-hand side, do you see the report that you made on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If we could just move to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you see your signature there, at the bottom of the page?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you see a name there, "Borislav Stankov"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Borislav Stankov was my supervisor. He was an electrical engineer and an expert in ballistics.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I tender this document into evidence, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will become P553, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, yesterday, when we described the role that you would play in these investigations, you said that you took photographs. Did you, on this occasion, take photographs of the incident site?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I took photographs of the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If I could ask that 65 ter 00193 be brought up on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you recognise, well, firstly, this photograph as the one that you took on the scene?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. That's the photograph of the place of impact of this explosive device.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If we could go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness 116, what do we see here on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this photograph, we see the house where the explosive device landed; and in the background, you can see the neighbouring houses in the same street.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And did the neighbouring houses sustain damage as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did. The roofs of the neighbouring houses were damaged and, of course, windows were broken, more precisely, the 11 neighbouring houses were rendered roofless.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, in my office before you testified, did you review these two photographs in addition to the series of photographs that you produced on this incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And do you recall that in that series of photographs there were two or three photographs of a deceased person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Did you take those photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Where did you take those photographs? Where was the person when you took the photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The persons had already been removed from the site, and they were in a makeshift mortuary set up within the compound of the mosque in Hrasnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, in the interest the time, I tender this series of photographs, if it is amenable to Your Honours, without going through each one individual.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: How many are there?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: There are about 31 of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Isailovic, any comments on that?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. According to my calculation, there should be 33 photographs. That would be right. And we know who has taken the photographs so we do not object to these photographs being tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll admit them.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P554, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I'm grateful to counsel for the advice.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I'm going to play a video for you, and I want you to first see it and then I'll ask you a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If I could have V000-7160 played in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise that location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, based on this single shot, I can't say that I do. You just started playing the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Okay. Well, we'll keep playing it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This is the house that had been hit by an explosive device.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And this house was destroyed in the investigation that you attended; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I just want you to confirm that the house we saw in this video was the house that was -- that sustained damage in the incident that you investigated on the 7th of April, 1995 in Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I tender that into evidence, this excerpt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P555, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I'm going to ask you about other investigations that you conducted. Firstly, do you recall investigating an incident on the 24th of May, 1995 at Safeta Zajke Street, number 43.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If I was to show you a map, would you be able to mark the location where you attended the investigation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Could I ask that 65 ter 2872 be brought up on the screen, please, and if the central part could be enlarged.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, on this map, can you see -- well, firstly, do you see the location of Safeta Zajke Street on that map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. It's situated in the left-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Perhaps the map could be -- we could scroll towards the -- fantastic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, if could you see the street, I would like you with the assistance of the court usher to mark the street where the incident occurred.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the street, Safeta Zajke Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And do you know whereabouts on that street the number 43 or where the incident occurred is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly speaking, in this area here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can I ask you just to put the letters SZ above that spot, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, in the investigation that you conducted, what -- what did you do when you got to the scene?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I arrived at the scene, the first thing I did was to make a broad overview of the scene; then I photographed the general area of the incident, and thereafter I photographed the place of impact of this explosive device. After that, I marked certain pieces of evidence with numbers; that is to say, fragments of the projectile, and other physical evidence that could be found around the place of impact; then I sketched the site, and I photographed also the damage sustained by the surrounding houses as a result of the impact.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you recall if there were any casualties in this incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were casualties.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Were these casualties civilian or military personnel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were all civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I'm going to show you a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Perhaps we can have this map tendered into evidence, although I would ask -- I'm going to ask the witness to make more markings on it, but it is probably better to have it tendered first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P556, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If I could now ask for --

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: -- 65 ter 73, 00073, and I'm interested in pages 25 to 28; and, again, it should not be broadcast, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, on the right-hand side of the screen, do you see a document, and do you see your name and signature there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. That's the sketch of the site which I made on the 24th of May, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I understand that the translation is not in e-court, but I do have hard copies for the benefit of the Bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please distribute them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If I could ask that we could move to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, is this the legend to the sketch that you compiled on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the legend.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If we could move to the next two pages and if they could be put side by side.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Is that the sketch that you drew, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you say from that sketch where the projectile landed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The projectile landed on Safeta Zajke Street. It's marked with number 1, and this is where the physical evidence were concentrated. That's the place of impact.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I tender these -- these pages into evidence, Mr. President, four pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We admit them.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P557, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These two pages of the sketch should be put together. These are actually two halves of one and the same sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I don't know if that is possible in terms of.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, it's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Perhaps the Prosecution could provide a free version to replace these two pages at a later date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Isailovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have the same question as yesterday. Could we number the pages of the 65 ter document, the pages that comprise document P554 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What are the pages, Mr. Sachdeva?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I believe I read them out when I asked for the pages to be brought up, but they are pages 25 to 28 of the composite exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, did you also produce an on-site forensic report for this incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Could I ask that pages 29 and 30 of exhibit -- 65 ter 73 be brought up, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The exhibit previously referred to is P557 and not P554.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, the translation should be in the bundle that was handed out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Is this your report, your forensic report, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: May we just go back to the first page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, I want you to look at this paragraph and in the penultimate sentence, it says -- it reads, "The projectile was fired from the south-east." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: On what basis did you include that in your report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I arrived at the scene, fragments of the projectile were on the asphalt surface of the street where it landed, and this is the part of the street where cars pass by. These fragments were embedded in the asphalt under a certain angle, indicating the south-easterly direction. It also made a funnel-shaped crater in the same direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Was it you who determined this? In other words, was it you who observed the funnel-shaped crater and determined the direction of fire, or were there other people in the team that did that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I established that. However, in most cases, we had ballistics experts on the team with us who gave the ultimate conclusion about the direction and origin of fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And was that the case in this instance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular instances, no, it wasn't. I don't think it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If we could go back to the map, please, the one that has just been marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, from the place where you've marked -- where you've marked that the incident took place, can you draw a line in the direction from which the projectile came; in other words, from south-east?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Approximately, like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I tender this map into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P558, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Prosecutor, could the witness be a little -- could the witness be a little bit more specific, please. The arrow showing this direction, what direction is it? South-east? South-west? North? We see an arrow, but did he not really explain anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, in your report, it's indicated that the direction of fire was south-east. Can you explain what this arrow represents ?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's something I assumed that it came approximately from that direction. I'm not completely sure that it came from that direction because I was a scene of the crime officer, not a forensic ballistics expert that could determine the trajectory precisely. My job was to make an on-site investigation of the scene, collect all the clues and evidence, all the fragments of shells, and all the other evidence related to the event. Determining the direction and the trajectory of the shell was not strictly my job.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Let me ask you, Witness, on this map, are you able to indicate north and south and east and west?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly, this is north, and this is south.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So in relation to that, where would south-east be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it would be like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So the first arrow you drew, to your knowledge, is that correct or incorrect?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you put a P at the bottom of the second arrow that you drew, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Does that clarify for Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would like to tender this map into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this map with the new markings will remain Exhibit P558.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: May I also tender pages 29 and 30 of 65 ter 73 into evidence, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be P559, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Could I ask that pages 31 and 32 from that same exhibit -- same 65 ter number be shown on the screen; again, not to be broadcast, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, do you see a document there on the screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And in the middle of document, do you see your name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: What is this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is an official report concerning the events of the 24th of May, 1995, when a modified air bomb landed, and it lists the persons present at the on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Does it relate to the incident at Safeta Zajke Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I tender this document under seal, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P560, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And, lastly, can I ask for 65 ter 73 to be shown on the screen; and for the benefit of counsel, that is pages 22 and 23 of the -- of 65 ter 73. There should be a translation for this, if you -- it's got a separate 65 ter number, 73H, which has the translation along with it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, do you see this document on the screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And what is this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is a report of the section for countersabotage protection, KDZ, and they accompany us scene of scene of crime officers on on-site investigations, to see whether there are any remaining explosive devices that could kill all the personnel that approaches the scene. They dug up the remnants of that projectile and provided their expertise for the fragments.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And the countersabotage protection, the KDZ, did that unit include ballistics experts to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ballistic forensic experts within the bomb squad, this section for countersabotage protection, know all about explosive devices; and based on parts of projectiles, they are able to recognise the type of shell. However, ballistic experts formed a separate section within the group of forensic experts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: This investigation report, does it relate to the incident at Safeta Zajke Street, number 43.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This report deals with that incident, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I tender this document into evidence, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P561, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, with respect to this incident, did you also take photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did for the photofile.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And were you given an opportunity look through these photographs before you testified?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: May I ask that 65 ter 00865 be brought up, please; again, not to be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Is that your signature, if you can read it, at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you see your name there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't see it. The printed part is not really legible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you see it now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Perhaps we can move to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Did you take these photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I made them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If the signature -- if you don't recognise the signature on the front page, whose signature was that? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recognise precisely whose signature it was, but I can explain one thing. The thing is that the people killed in this incident were transported to a mortuary on the other end of town, and that's why photographs were made of the bodies. And another part of my team of scene of the crime officers took the photographs of bodies. I probably provided my part of the report and they provided theirs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So in this series of photographs, the ones of the scene were taken by you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I took photographs of the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And in this series of photographs, the photographs of the bodies, who were they taken by?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Was it someone in your department?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Why didn't you take photographs of the bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not photograph the bodies because the hospital, together with the mortuary, were on the other end of town. On that day, the shelling was intense; and, at that time, I was at the police station in that part of up to be able to more efficiently cover that part of Novi Grad municipality where the shell landed. Moving around was very dangerous during intense shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So despite the fact that you don't have your signature on the front page and you weren't able to discern your name, can you confirm to the Court that the photographs of the scene were taken by you on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I am certain that I made these photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And the photographs taken of the bodies in the mortuary by a colleague from your department, can you confirm that they were also official photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, they are official photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I tender these photographs into evidence, Mr. President, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: They are admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P562, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, on that day, on the 24th of May, 1995, did you also -- did you investigate another incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On that day, as I said before, there was intense shelling on Sarajevo, especially the Novi Grad municipality where I was at the police station, and that's why I didn't go to other locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And the incident that you investigated, where did that incident occur?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That incident occurred at a location overlooking the transformer station in Novi Grad municipality, also providing for Novo Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you remember the location or the name of the street or the location where the transformer station was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember -- normally, I remember, but the name of the street eludes me at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Did you produce a sketch when you went to the investigation for this incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I took photographs of the scene and a sketch as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Could I ask that page -- page 9 of 65 ter 00076 be brought up, please; again, not to be broadcast. Mr. President, might I inquire how much time I have left?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I have to say none. You are now at the discretion of the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: May I therefore ask leave to continue for a further five to eight minutes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, is this a sketch -- is this the first page of the sketch that you produced?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And do you see where it says, "Mjesto"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mjesto and Majdanska Street. The location is Majdanska Street, no number, transformer station Novi Grad.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Could we just go to the next three pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, just have a look and confirm that this is indeed your sketch and your legend.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There is the key and the description of events.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: The next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Is that the sketch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a sketch, the sketch of the scene where the projectile landed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I would ask that pages 9, 10, 11, and 12 be admitted into evidence, under seal, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P563, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Did you also produce an on-site report, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. I did an on-site report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Could we move to page 5 of this 65 ter number, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Is this your on-site investigation report, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And do you see at the end of the paragraph, does it give a direction from which the projectile came?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says the projectile came from the area of Paljevac, south-east.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can we move back to the map, please, which is Exhibit --

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: -- 558. Actually, there should be another.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, while we're waiting for the right map to show up, could you please ask the witness if he is able to indicate or to identify the kind of projectile that landed on the 24th of May?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, with respect to the incident at the transformer station, do you know what type of projectile exploded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what type of projectile exploded, but I know for a fact that it had huge destructive power, made an enormous hole in the ground and vast damage to surrounding buildings. It was probably a modified air bomb, because not a single projectile of smaller calibre could have produced such huge devastation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may. Unfortunately, we don't have the markings that were made the second time around on the map. We're unable to locate them at this time. Perhaps the counsel would like to have the witness to make the markings again, and we can resave the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That is unfortunate. Well, let that be down.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, unfortunately, due a technical hitch, the initial markings that you made were not recorded. Can you again start by indicating north, south, east, and west.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And from the location where -- and this refers to the incident at Safeta Zajka Street, can you draw an arrow or a line in the direction from which the projectile came; that is, south-east, as contained in your report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well. If you want me to, I can indicate the place where the projectile landed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Well, first, I want you to indicate the direction from which the projectile came with respect to the Safeta Zajke incident, the first incident, because those markings have unfortunately been -- have not been recorded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What is the arrow which --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, that is not what you indicated first. Well, I would say not generally.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps can I explain because the witness did say, "Very well. If you want me to, I can indicate the place where the projectile landed." In other words, I submit he is referring to this present case, this present incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, you see where you have written SZ there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And that stands for Safeta Zajke Street, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's Safeta Zajke Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And do you recall in your report that you produced the direction of fire for that incident was recorded as south-east; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And a moment ago you indicated with an arrow that direction. Do you remember doing that beforehand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Unfortunately, that was not recorded. Can you do that again now, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And just to be clear for this exhibit, the arrow that you have -- the horizontal arrow above the one that you have just drawn, is that a correct or incorrect depiction of the direction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't exactly reflect the direction from which the projectile came.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: The arrow that you have just drawn, can you put a P underneath that, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Why don't have you him delete the arrow which doesn't depict the direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I had thought about that, but my understanding was that that -- that is evidence which Defence might want to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see. They might want to refer to that. Okay. Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, now can you mark -- with respect to Majdanska, the transformer station, can you mark the location where the projectile landed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's been deleted. I marked it twice, but after a few seconds the colour just vanishes. It's been deleted, but now I have marked it with colour blue.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm sorry, but have I an objection regarding the colour, because I intend to ask the witness to mark this map with blue. Maybe there's a third colour available for Defence, but it would nice if Prosecution could stick to red.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, yes. Well, you have a patent on blue, so select another colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I didn't -- I actually didn't ask for it to be blue, so I'd like to continue in red.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It has been deleted again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, maybe use another colour, but not blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I think now it seems to be working.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: If I may, it probably problem appears to be that when the witness is marking on the SMART Board, he is holding down the pen and moving it. If he could be directed to mark it and then remove the pen immediately.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Fabulous. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, Can you just put the letter M by that spot and be sure to remove the pen as soon as you have finished.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And the arrow that you have drawn, the one without the P towards the bottom of the page, is that the direction of fire for this incident in Majdanska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. If you want me, I can put a letter M next to this arrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes, that would be fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I ask that this be tendered into evidence, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P564, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Might I just inquire that it has been recorded? Thank you. If we can move to page 7 of 65 ter 76, I think it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, is this an expert report for that incident at Majdanska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. The expert analysis was conducted by the KDZ department relating to the incident of the 25th of May, 1995, which took place on Majdanska Street, no number.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Does it say 25th or 24th of May?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, 24th. But the report was compiled on the 25th.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I tender that into evidence, Mr. President. That's pages 7 and 8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P565, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And, lastly, pages 1 -- sorry, pages 2, 3, and 4 I'm interested in of this same ter number.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, do you see this document and do you see your name in the middle there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: What is this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an official report of the Ministry of the Interior on the incident that took place on the 24th of May, 1995 on Safeta Zajke Street outside number 43 and on Majdanska Street, no number, on which occasion four people were killed and 11 other people were injured.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And do you recognise this document to be an official report from the CSB? Can you confirm that it is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I tender this under seal, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Isailovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Just to be useful, I believe that this document has already been admitted as a P560, and it was also admitted at P313. So maybe it would be better to check right now, to make sure that we don't have any mix-ups. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, thank you for that. There is a very fortunate document to be admitted, what, twice and now its admission is being sought a third time. Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's not entirely clear what portions of this document have been admitted, and the notes in e-court, on March 2nd, portions of this document were admitted. It says that the admission should top with ERN number 75126 and not include the rest of the medical report. However, it's unclear exactly what that means.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll admit it and note the possible duplication.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes P566.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it was admitted earlier as P560 just a few minutes ago. It was admitted as P560. I will use it, which is why I'm taking role of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is that so, Mr. Court Deputy?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: As I understand it, I asked for particular pages of the ter number to be admitted, and this particular document is pages 2 and 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see. What was admitted then was a different set of pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Let us proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, did you produce photographs on this incident? Witness, did you hear my question? I asked you if you produced photographs with respect to Majdanska Street.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did make photographs, but I was hoping to see them on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I'm going to show you now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Could I have 65 ter 0076 brought up on the screen now, please. Can I withdraw that, please. Excuse me. I withdraw that question and in fact the photographs for this incident have been tendered already. I'm now going to move to the final incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, do you remember investigating an incident on the 16th of June, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Was this incident at Trg Medjunarodnog Prijateljstva?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is where it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And, similarly, did you produce an on-site report, a sketch, and did you take photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I produced an on-site report, took photographs, and drew a sketch of the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can I ask that 65 ter number 132 be brought up, And I'm interested in the first seven pages. Move to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, do you see a document on the screen; and if you do, can you tell us -- tell the Court what it is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an Official Note produced by the Novi Grad public security station of the Ministry of the Interior. It relates to an incident which took place on the 16th of June, 1995 at 1520 hours on the street Trg Medjunarodnog Prijateljstva, number 10, where a modified air bomb exploded and slightly injured seven persons but inflicted substantial material damage on the surrounding buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you. And in the next paragraph, do you see your name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I tender this document, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P567, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That will be page 2 of the 65 ter of 132. Can we now move to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, is this your on-site investigation report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can we move to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Is that your name and signature there at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is my name and my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I tender enter pages 3 and 4 of 132, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P568, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And, Witness, I'm now going to show you a sketch, the sketch, and this is pages 5, 6 and 7. And if you can just confirm that this is indeed the sketch that you took, that you drew on that incident.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the sketch that I made in relation to this incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can we see pages 5 and 6, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Is that the legend?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, this is the legend.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I tender pages 5, 6, and 7, under seal, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We admit them.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P569, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Lastly, Witness - and this is my final question - did you take photographs of this incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I made a few photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Could I ask that 65 ter 00076 be brought up.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: My apologies. I think it's ter number 133.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Are these the photographs that you took, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are the photographs, and in them one can clearly see the corner of a multi-story building. It has more than ten floors and the projectile of such an a devastating and destructive power, if it had hit the building, it would have demolished it completely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Mr. President, I tender these documents into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P570, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Isailovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness. I'm Branislava Isailovic, a lawyer with the Paris Bar, and I defend General Dragomir Milosevic accused in these proceedings, and I'm go to ask you a few questions. I would like to start with the statements that you discussed yesterday with the Prosecutor. Do you remember having done this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: You made four statements to the Office of the Prosecutor. First one on November 14, 1995, a document that was admitted as P548. In this statement, you mention about your work methods. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a protected witness with a pseudonym, so I would like the document to be called up on screen but not be broadcast. Can we move to page 2 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you're talking about your training. I noted that you were trained for your police work during a six-month session. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: You started your job in August 1993. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But initially I attended the scene with a senior technician in order to become more knowledgeable about the practicality aspects of the job.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, at first you were a junior technician and you were always working with a senior technician.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us when you started doing your on-site investigations alone.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I started doing my own investigations in late 1993 and early 1994. I attended the scenes of minor offences, such as burglaries and things like that; in other words, minor criminal offences.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: When you started -- when did you start going to on -- when did you start working on on-site investigations alone on more serious offences?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, during 1993, or rather, during 1994, that is to say, late 1994 and 1995. But I have to say that whenever some serious incident took place, I always went with a senior technician; and with us there was always, even in minor incidents, we had criminal investigation inspectors and also there was judge go a major incident was involved. And if there were fatalities, there were Court-appointed experts. There were also ballistics experts -- court appointed ballistics experts, as well as members of the staff of the KDZ primarily to provide security for us as a team and to check whether there were any unexploded devices.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. I think you have answered.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, all these people you mentioned, were their names included in the reports?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, as a rule.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So whenever the investigating magistrate was there, his name would be written among the people in charge of the investigation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. However, I didn't include the names. I was focussed only on the technical aspects of the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know the investigating magistrate personally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not personally. I knew them by sight only. I wasn't close to them or on friendly terms with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: How often do you remember having seen an investigating magistrate that you would know at least by sight.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean outside my work?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry. I'm thinking about seeing this investigating magistrate on-site, where you were actually carrying out an investigation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Whenever there was a serious incident, such as shelling involving a large number of casualties or serious casualties, the whole team would be there, including a judge and UN observers, frequently. UN observers wanted to see with their own eyes what was going on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We have to take the break now. We'll break for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Isailovic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, we will continue on the same topic. So I would like to talk about your work methods as criminal technician on site. Could you please take a look at the page that is on the screen in front of you, and you can use it, of course, to refreshing your memory, if need be. So you were saying that you would always go on site together with the team members, and you would take pictures on site. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. The team could number a smaller or larger number of people, but there was always a team.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Among the team members, which one was telling you what pictures to take?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I alone chose which photographs to take, while members of my team would point certain things out to me, things that I may have overlooked, or things I needed to pay special attention to, so that we viewed the crime scene all together. And we all together tried to find clues, evidence, put them on the sketch, and photograph them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Today, we have been able to see a number of photographs that were taken by you. So on the basis of these photographs which we saw and which we might see again today, could you tell me what kind of selection criteria you used when you took these pictures and when you photographed everything that was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The classic procedure, the traditional procedure in conducting an on-site investigation is to inspect the scene broadly and to talk with uniformed policemen securing it, those who were on the scene first, because they have the first basic information about the incident, such as what happened, what the casualties are, et cetera. So there is an interview with them, inspection of the broader area of the scene, photographing of the broader area, photographing of the scene itself without moving any objects, without tampering with the scene in any way. After that, numbers are given to various pieces of evidence. Each piece of evidence is photographed separately, and a measuring tape is placed against evidence to show the exact size and dimensions. After that, when a sketch is made, my first task was to find a basic point of reference, such as the corner of a building, a solid object that is not likely to change in the years to come, and then the distance from that point of reference to various pieces of evidence is taken. On the basis of photographs and the sketch, then a report is made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just one moment. The question was: "What kind of selection criteria did you use?" You seem to be explaining how you took the photographs. Could you concentrate on the question which was the kind of selection. How did you select the photographs to be taken.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, let me ask, Ms. Isailovic. What did you mean by "the selection criteria"?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, what I meant by "selection criteria" was the fact that one chooses one object rather than another. So you photograph a house, for instance, and you don't photograph the house that's next door. You don't photograph the damage caused to a particular building and not to another, because we have seen the pictures that were taken by the witness. So it's a matter of understanding who determined which criteria to apply. So this was my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. So was he answering your question?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, that's what I --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You quite rightly noticed it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: When the witness is not answering your question, you should stop him when he is not answering the question. So do you understand what she is asking? Why would you decide to photograph a particular house as against the house that is next door, that is it next to it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I photographed the place where the shell landed and the houses around it that were damaged by the explosion.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] .

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, how did you know what kind of damage was caused by the explosion which you were investigating?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know what kind of damage was involved, but it was obvious that a house was destroyed, half of the roof was missing, all the windows shattered, lots of shrapnel in the walls. When you are in a situation like that, it is evident that you are in a place where something evil was done.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to illustrate this with an example. A while ago, we've seen the pictures that were taken of Hrasnica on the 7th of April, 1995. Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: At the time you reached the site, were you aware of other explosions that had taken place in Hrasnica before the 7th of April, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was aware, because all of Sarajevo had been shelled for four years by that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Precisely, Witness. How did you establish a distinction between the damage caused, let's call it the explosion we are talking -- we are currently talking about, the one which you came to investigate, and the damage caused by the previous explosions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The spot where this projectile landed was one where two houses were completely destroyed, and it blew up the roofs of 11 other houses. It was an inhabited area.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I shall follow the instructions of the President of the Chamber. This was not my question. How could you establish a distinction in Hrasnica between the damage caused by the explosion we are talking about, the one that took place on the 7th of April, 1995, and the other explosions that occurred before that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at the end of the day, I could not distinguish, but it was my duty as a scene-of-crime officer to photograph the location, to enable later reconstruction, because whatever crime is committed photographs of all the surrounding buildings have to be made in order to enable a reconstruction.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you have conducted other investigations on-site, according to your statements and according to what have you told us today. So you were able to determine where the shot came from or where it was fired from. So how did you establish a distinction between the damage caused and the explosions that occurred? So what did you do to determine the origin of fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a difficult question. However, this projectile had enormous destructive power, and it created a scale of devastation that I had not seen before that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I noticed that on the photographs you took, which have now been tendered into evidence, you drew some arrows; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, what do these arrows stand for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These arrows show the most probable direction from which the projectile came.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And who drew these arrows?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: You draw these areas --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could you kindly repeat your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have been asked to repeat my question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: This refers to the time the arrows were drawn. Was it at the time you were developing your photographs? Because I assume you were taking the pictures with a camera, and I assume you weren't able to draw the arrows on the same day. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I used a still camera, and what is made on the spot is a rough sketch. That's when I placed the arrows, because I heard from the uniformed policemen on the spot that there were witnesses, eye-witnesses, who had seen from which direction the projectile had come. That's something that I wasn't able to determine.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. I would also like to know at what point in time you drew these arrows.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the moment when I arrived at the scene to perform the on-site investigation. After the on-site investigation, I must have gotten back to my office, sat down, made that sketch, and made the lines with a ruler to make it look better; whereas, the rough sketch was made on the spot.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I shall repeat my question. So, you took your pictures with a camera on site; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And when you look at these two photographs, you can see that there are some arrows on them; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And in order to draw these arrows, you need to have a support medium, i.e., a photograph, don't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And what I'm interested in is the following: Between the time you take the picture and the time you develop your photograph, how long does it take?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One day.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And now what I'm interested in is the following: The next day -- on the next day, you looked at other reports before drawing your arrows on the photographs, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I did not look at other reports. I was doing my job.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I would now like to get back to what you said a while ago. You said you cross-questioned the policemen who had questioned the eye-witnesses in order to determine the direction of fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And what I'm interested in is this: Was this procedure written down anywhere or mentioned in any of your reports?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I am now going to ask you a few questions about some of the victims you were able to see on the site. First of all, were you able to see them there or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not. The victims had already been removed from the site and placed in a mortuary. The mortuary was close by.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I'm talking as a matter of principle. I'm not talking about any particular incident. So as a rule, were the victims on the site?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the moment when I arrived with my team, there were no longer any victims on the site.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement, you mention the fact that these victims have a particular status. You have talked about them being civilians, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Da. [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And on these occasions, how could you establish the status of these people, either as civilians or members of the army? What did you do to establish their status?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you see a 50-year-old woman dressed in civilian clothing, I think it would be obvious to anyone that she was not a soldier.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And when you see a man wearing ordinary clothes, what do you think of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So what criterion or criteria did you establish a distinction between the two?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not my job to determine who was a civilian and who was military. My job was to determine on site all the facts on the spot.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Precisely. So that wasn't part of your job, but, nonetheless, you talk about it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in the report, you write the names of the casualties or victims.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So can one say that you didn't look into this question; in other words, you didn't ask yourself when you saw a victim whether this person was a civilian or a member of the army when you prepared your reports?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, in your various statements, when you mentioned civilians or army members, you didn't apply any particular criteria to establish this distinction. This was just something that you were inferring.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My part of the job was technical.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I'd like to turn to page 3 of the statement. This is your statement, and you mention this particular incident in Hrasnica that took place on the 7th of April, 1995. First of all, I'd like to know how you got to Hrasnica and on what day.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I just see that page on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: It's going to come up any minute now. This document is already on the screen. This is page 3 of document 3108, a 65 ter document.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day I was on duty, and the police administration in Ilidza that was based there Hrasnica called up the Security Services Centre --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry. For the sake of efficiency, was it on the same day as the explosion, as far as you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. On that same day, we arrived.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember at what time this was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We arrived around 3.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember having seen the UNMO representatives on the spot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were there with two APCs.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Were these UNPROFOR APCs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Do you make a difference between UNPROFOR soldiers and UNMOs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you one thing: At the moment, I was not able to distinguish between them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Did you actually see soldiers whom you believed were UNMOs carrying out the same investigation as you on the scene?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: According to what you remember, did you get to the scene on the next day; namely, the 8th of April, 1995? That's the day when you reach Hrasnica. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We came to inspect the scene once again and to try to find some more evidence, if possible. We were just double-checking.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: But did you see UNMOs at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement, the one you have before you, you state that on the next day you found other pieces of evidence on the site. This is on paragraph 2, and you say on the next day -- it's not very clear. On the next day, you came along with two UNMOs. Is this right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva. Let me here from Mr. Sachdeva first.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps it is confusing. However in the English translation, which is the version that the witness signed, it says that on the day of the event we arrived together with two United Nations Military Observers. My submission is that the event refers to the incident and not the next day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I've checked this, Your Honour, and I tend to look at the B/C/S version. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So you said on the first day the UNMOs were on the site.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same reads in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement in B/C/S, and this is what is confusing, you mention the next day, which is the day you found pieces of evidence. Are you with me? Do you see this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: To that -- this could be confusing, because you say that the day you saw the UNMOs conducting the investigation was on the 7th of April. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It's clearly written here on the day of the incident we arrived together with two UNMOs. However, UNMOs were present there on a daily basis, and they had full insight into the situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Of course, Witness, you did not find the victims on the site on the 7th of April, 1995, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement, thereafter, you mention eye-witnesses to this incident. It wasn't part of your job to take witness statements, was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. My job was strictly technical. Criminal investigation police inspectors were duty-bound to take witness statements.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: In the paragraph that starts with, "Bomba je dosla," is this something that you were able to establish yourself or is this something that you established on the basis of witness statements?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't have determined that on my own. It could only have been done based on the statements given by the uniformed policemen securing the scene.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I would like you to read everything that comes after the sentence starts with, "Bomba je dosla," until the portion which mentions the incident of the 7th of April, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, just so I am clear, counsel has said the paragraph starting, and she has used B/C/S. I'm not entirely sure if that could be translated into English, so I know exactly which paragraph she is referring to. I presume it is when it starts about the direction of north-west, but I just want to be clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Would you just clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This is the paragraph which starts in the middle of the page, "The bomb came," in English, and "Bomba je dosla," in B/C/S, which is also in the middle of the page. So this ends with: "I also drew," and in B/C/S, "Takodjersam na karti." So I have asked the witness to look at this portion of his statement, and I shall put questions to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: This part of your statement describes the launch of the bomb and the direction it took. Can we saw today that this is solely based on hearsay and is not based on your findings an investigation on the site?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, based on hearsay and not on my own investigation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: You will the opportunity to see a video that was filmed by a BBC reporter, and you admitted that this had to do with the incident you investigated in -- the incident that occurred in Hrasnica on the 7th of April, 1995, the incident you investigated together with an entire team. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to know what details made it possible for you to be so sure that this is actually dealing with this incident that occurred on that day.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because it shows total destruction of the house where the projectile landed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Was it the only house entirely destroyed that you saw during your work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I hadn't seen a case like this before. This must have been a very heavy bomb.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You should attend more carefully to the question, which was: "Was it the only house entirely destroyed that you saw during your work?" What's the answer to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw many houses on fire, many houses damaged by tank shells, but this kind of destruction I had never seen before.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Now, normally, when you arrive on site when an incident has occurred, I would like to know whether you ever possibly envisaged that the bomb might have been planted there and would have exploded right there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: This hypothesis was never envisaged by the investigators.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because the aggressor tried to promote this hypothesis in Sarajevo very often, but it is very naive to believe that people would be shelling themselves for four years. I think that would be an exaggeration.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: The word used by the witness was not "exaggeration" but "naive." It would be "naive."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both "exaggerate" and "naive."

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So it was -- it would have been naive. So this hypothesis was ruled out from the very start. When you started working in 1994 and further, you always ruled that hypothesis out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, over two million shells landed in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you have another statement dated February 26th, 1996, 65 ter document number 3109. We'll go through this quickly. It's a question that the Prosecutor did not address with you, but the statement has been admitted into evidence. First, do you recognise your statement dated February 26th, 1996?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And if we could please move to page 2 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I'm interested in paragraph 2. You are mentioning an incident that occurred on November 8, 1994, a sniping incident. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: In the English version of the statement, there is a third page. Unfortunately, it has not been translated, but this is a report. Personally, I would not have called this a forensic report, as is said in the translation. I believe that this is a report on the search that occurred on site.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we could move to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: First, do you see your signature on this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
