utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please go back to the previous page, because here I have a slight problem with the birth date of this victim.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at this, and could you please read out that sentence?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For English speakers, I'm mentioning the first paragraph and I'm asking the witness to read out the first paragraph starting with: "Dana."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: "At around 1530, on 8th November 1994, in the flat owned by Sabahita Omerovic on 9/5, Djura Danatica [phoen] Street, the fifth floor, Nermina Omerovic was killed. She was born on the 31st of October, 1994." Now, this is me speaking. I made a mistake here. She was born on the 31st of October, 1984. So we're talking about a girl, who was at the time 10 years old.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: When did you note that you had made a mistake -- there was a mistake?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I noted it just now. If you look at the photograph of the body, you can determine the age of the girl.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you can confirm that your reports were used to establish the criminal liability of the alleged offenders.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And when reading this report, which you would like to correct today in this court, don't you find that there is an inconsistency in this report, because here it would be a baby rather than a 10-year-old that is mentioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is possible, and it was my mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember where this happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember where this happened. This building is very close to River Miljacka, which was a separation line between the Bosnian side and the aggressor. The windows were covered with thin plywood. The girl opened the door for a minute and shut it when the bullet passed through the window and killed her.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that on the basis of a conversation with her family when I came there for the reconstruction of the incident.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Did you take pictures of the victim of this incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could we please look at your statement on the second page. First, could we say that you were just starting your job as a technician working on your own, in November 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Here you are telling how you proceed to establish the direction the shot came from, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I answer your question?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I came to attend the reconstruction of the incident. It was not me who determined the direction from which the shot had come. It was, rather, done by the ballistic experts, Mr. Mirza Sabljica, a mechanical engineer, and Borislav Stankov, an electrical engineer and court-pointed expert witness, who was my supervisor. Both of them were ballistics experts, and it was them who determined that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, but you were an eye-witness to these investigations carried out by your more senior colleagues, and you were talking about two panels, two plywood panels, that were placed on the windows?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: What was the distance between these two panels?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A few centimetres.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: You're saying a few centimetres, because of what? How was this construction applied to the windows?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a rather old building from the era of Austria-Hungary. The buildings were old and had two wings. During the war, the windows were broken. The residents remitted the plywood panels in order to enable them to live in these rooms.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I have a very technical question, so please think about it in technical terms and as a technician. You're saying that out of the two holes in the two panels, your colleagues were able to establish the direction the bullet came from. That's it, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was also a bullet trace on the floor. They stretched a string between the place where the bullet landed on the floor and the hole in the plywood panel. So they established the direction from which the bullet had come. After that, and I was looking what they were -- watching what they were doing although this was not part of my job, they viewed through a tube and one can precisely determine the point of origin of the gunshot. My task under those circumstances was to open the window, risk my life in so doing, and photograph the building where the gunshot came from, and this is what I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Does this document exist somewhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I photographed the adjacent building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Isailovic, you must conclude by the end of this session.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just like my colleague, I will ask by your leave ask to you give me some extra time. I mean, the Prosecution required twice the time that was allocated. So if I'm allowed the same thing, I would need three hours. I don't need three hours, of course, but I do have a great number of questions to ask because that this is a very important witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The Prosecution used an hour and 44 minutes, and you would have used the same time by the end of the session. If you wish, you can have another -- how many minutes more would you wish?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can do what my colleague did and ask for five and go on for 40. I can give you an estimate, of course. I don't exactly when the session is supposed to end, in 25 minute, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, please continue, and we can deal with it when we come to the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, let's take a look at the Sarajevo map, document 65 ter 104.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, 2872.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Now the map is on display.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the court officer please zoom into the Marindvor area, where the Holiday Inn is located on the right, where Grbavica is located, and really zoom into that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please look at the map and tell us where the building where this victim was hit is located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this area here.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see the area where the -- where you photographed the building which was allegedly the source -- the origin of fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That building is not drawn on this map, but it's directly opposite.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: You determined this building to be Metalka, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: According to you, the building located in front is Metalka.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark an I, November 8, 1994. So next to the mark that you have just placed, Witness, could you please use the electronic pen and mark a letter I, as "incident," next to the mark that you have already put on the map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And below that I, could you please write 8/11/94, for the date of the incident.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to tender this as a Defence exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it's admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D166, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you give us a rough estimate of the distance between this building and Metalka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three hundred metres at the outside.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: At the time, did you know that units of the ABiH army were located in this area next to this building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I'd like to have the same map as annotated by the witness. It's P564. Could we have this on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to talk about other incidents, the two incidents that occurred on the same day on May 24, 1995, in two different places. The SZ that you marked corresponds to the place where, allegedly, you say that the air bomb exploded on Safeta Zajke Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, approximately, that's the place.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: On this map, you noted the -- you noted where the south, north, east, and west is. And did you use these type of coordinates when you were trying to establish where the fire came from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you: We were told where the fire came from, and I did use the coordinates, but that's roughly it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: You say, "We were told where the shot came from." Who is that "we," please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For instance, forensic experts, ballistic experts, and people from the bomb squad. They would be the ones who determined more precisely where the projectile had come from.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I thought I understood that in your reports, in the report that you drafted yourself, you always noted the direction of the shot.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So is it fair to say that you used information you got from the other members of the team?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So these were not your own findings using the traces found on site.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I have to say when a projectile fired from a mortar or a cannon or some type of artillery piece falls, it leaves a pretty clear trace, showing from which direction it had been fired. However, with modified air bombs, that is much more difficult, and we determined the direction based on the funnel-shaped crater. But the most important factor were eye-witnesses who had seen it flying, because the modified air bomb was very slow flying through the air and it could be seen with a naked eye. Once, when such a bomb fell outside the building of the municipality of Novi Grad, I saw it myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: What exactly did you see that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in Safeta Zajke Street?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: No. I'm talking about the time where you personally saw the flight of this projectile that you're calling an air bomb.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It looks like a small aircraft, moving very slowly and producing very strange, wheezing sound, and can you see it with the naked eye.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Is there a smoke trail, possibly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw that projectile when it was already going down, and there was no trace of smoke.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So -- but there was no smoke trail that would still be lingering on in the sky, as can you see, for example, when there is a plane that is in the sky.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the case I have seen, there was no trace of smoke. It was already going down, and I was perhaps 200 metres from the place where it fell.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: What was the flight path when this projectile was falling? Was it falling straight? How did it fall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was falling in a slant. In physics, it's called a slanted hit.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could you please allow the witness to sketch this on a piece of paper, and I would like to tender the sketch, if you allow for it, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, he may do that. Just a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, could you draw what you were showing us with your hands earlier, you know, what you saw when this projectile fell. The actual path of this projectile when it fell.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Now, to be specific, you were able to see this part of the trajectory or the path of this projectile.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw only the end of the path.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And therefore behind the projectile, there was no smoke, or smoke trail?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. I didn't see any trace of smoke.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now could I please have an exhibit number for this sketch, and if you could just write in B/C/S, "avio bomba."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I could just add.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. It may be numbered.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is will be D167.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I could add one thing, if I may?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, what's that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This modified air bomb produced a terrible noise during its flight. It sounded like some sort of destruction, a very strange high-pitched sound, and everybody to hear it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Isailovic, I would just have a question for clarification sake. Witness, this particular sketch relates to what incident in particular?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This relates to the incident, an on-site investigation, when an air bomb fell outside the building of the municipality of Novi Grad, between the municipal building and the radio television Bosnia-Herzegovina building.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour and Judges of the Bench, this was one of the incidents that was listed on the incident list; but pursuant to your order, this incident has been taken off the list. This is the one dated 29th of June. Now, I am about to move on to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, if indeed it is that incident, does that entitle the Prosecution to -- does it open up for the Prosecution to ask questions on that, since the Defence has led evidence on this incident?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I respond to the Prosecution's request? I did not ask this particular question in relation to any particular incident but in relation to this witness's testimony, because he told us that he was an eye-witness to the fall of an air bomb.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Since the evidence relates to a dropped incident, it will be ignored. No account will be taken of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, let's have a look now at your third statement, the one what is dated the 11th --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. President. Does that mean that pursuant to your order that the sketch is not going to be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, that should also be deleted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, D167 will be removed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I would now like to turn to your statement dated 11th of March, 1997.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a 65 ter document number 3110. Let's go straight to page 3, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned two incidents. First of all, one incident that took place on the 16th of June, 1995, but you conducted the investigation on this particular site ten days later; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: An official report was issued after these investigations. You addressed this with the Prosecutor a while ago. We are now talking about document 132, a 65 ter document, page 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, do you remember why nobody went on the site on the day and that the people only went there ten days later?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember, because the shelling was intense those days, and it was very dangerous to go out into clear space and we went out there only when the situation calmed down a bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Isailovic, we have come to the time for the break. In ten minutes the court deputy informs me you will have used exactly the same time as the Prosecutor. And how much more time would you need, beyond that ten minutes and do not tell me that you can, like the Prosecutor, ask for five and be given on half an hour, because I will consider that out of order. How much more time will you need?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, given the importance of this witness for us and for the Prosecution that has been granted extra time by the Bench, I feel it would be fair that I have enough time to. Begin with, we talked about an hour, hour and a half. I have now had the same time as the Prosecution, and I believe that half an hour is, at best, what I would need.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, all right. We'll give you half an hour. We'll take the break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, we were working on a document that was admitted as P567.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we could have something else, because right now we have got the English version on both sides.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Just to ensure that it's not going broadcast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please ensure it's not being broadcast, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, this is an Official Note after an event which occurred on June 16, 1995. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you confirm that in the second paragraph of this document the following is said: "The investigation was made on June 26th, 1995."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you also confirm that this memo is dated ten days -- is dated on the 16th of June, ten days offer the event?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but in the second paragraph below it says: "Due to intense shelling of the entire neighbourhood, it was not possible to conduct an on-site investigation. So on the 26th of June, 1995, at 9.00 a.m., the complete team came out on site," et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, earlier, you confirmed that this memo came -- was an official document from the Bosnian police, which is why I'm asking this question. Why is it that we have a document drafted on June 16, 1995, where there is mention of events that will occur ten days later?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The crime investigations inspector, Mujo Music, who made the minutes, made an error; but from the text below, one can see how this investigation on site progressed and what the situation was like.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, the dates were an important information for the Bosnian police, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, extremely important.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And yet earlier we noted that there had been a mistake regarding the date of birth of one of the victims.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But that mistake becomes obvious when you read through the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So, according to you, it would be not fabricating documents and then placing the dates for another reason than for investigation reasons. Would that be something that could be envisaged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, actually, I withdraw that and perhaps I would like to hear the answer of the witness. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that we heard the answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is not conceivable.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you go on, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was saying it's not conceivable the documents were forged or tampered with because a large number of people were involved in those teams for on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So, according to you, this memo was drafted after June 26, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. The inspector who made this note made a perfectly appropriate note, apart from the fact that in the heading, he mistyped the date. But from the text of this note, since it follows a chronological order, it is clear how the events developed and what the sequence of events was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: According to you, Witness, does this memo take into account the results of the investigations that were carried out after the incident? And I'm especially thinking about the direction of fire.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This Official Note shows only the state of affairs, the factual aspect, when the shell landed, how many people were hurt, who the members of the on-site investigation team were, and at 9.00 on the 26th of June when that investigation took place. It also mentioned the size of the resulting crater and the people injured during the explosion. So this is purely a detailed description of the event.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, in paragraph 3, can you find the place where it is stated that the shot probably came from Lukavica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't really understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Can you read paragraph 3, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: In this memo, it is said that the -- that the possible origin of fire was from the aggressor's position in Lukavica. Is that what's written?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's written there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether these were also your findings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the projectile landed, it made a huge funnel-shaped crater and it came from the direction of Lukavica. I mean, the crater was pointed to the direction of Lukavica. There were also ballistics experts with me on the team and other experts as well who arrived at this conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we could please have page 3 of this document, document 65 ter 132, which was given the exhibit number P568. It's difficult to read, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: But if could you please try and read when it starts with, "najvjero vatnije."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The missile in question was most probably a modified aircraft bomb with four in-built rocket engines and great destructive force. It came from the direction of," I cannot see this clearly here, "from the aggressor's positions."

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, first, could the court officer please zoom into this part, because I can guess what is written and the interpreter who translated the document --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see the right hand part.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: In the English translation of this document, the direction is as follows: "Aggressor's position from the west." Maybe the interpreter had a more legible copy. I'm not sure. But can you confirm that it is written exactly what I said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So these were your findings after the investigations which Detective Music took into account?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. However, I say that this was most probably a modified air bomb, so I didn't put it directly and specifically what kind of an explosive device was involved.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could my case manager please display 65 ter document 2872, the Sarajevo map, and we must find ...

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So we will find this area called "Medjunarodnog Prijateljstva." And if we could please zoom into the area in the bottom of the map, we see Novi Grad and Lukavica. Could you please show us where this incident occurred at Trg Medjunarodnog. Could you take the pen, Witness, please, and I would kindly ask the usher to assist you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please zoom in a little bit? The central part of the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a little, because we would like to locate Lukavica after that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see it now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where Lukavica is?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, draw a circle around Lukavica and then Trg Medjunarodnog Prijateljstva.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: In any case, we can say that Medjunarodnog Prijateljstva is at Alipasino Polje; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's part of Alipasino Polje.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Now, in relation to this circle, first of all, could you place the letter I, for "incident" next to it. TMP, please, on the small circle; and I, for "incident." Yes, that's fine. That's fine. That tells us where the street is. Now, the second circle, could you plays the letter L next to the second circle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And could you draw a line from the small circle to the west.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you place the letter W here; W stands for "west."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Please, on this line --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I made a mistake. [In English] Yes. [Interpretation] This is east.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: In that case, you can delete the W line and draw a line in -- towards the west and place the letter W there, please. Please correct your mistake.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: W, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to tender this map into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D167, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you remember that you discussed another incident with the Prosecution which took place in the Safeta Zajke Street.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. I didn't wait for the exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be D167, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you discussed the incident that took place on 24th of May, 1995, Safeta Zajke with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to now see the 65 ter document 865. This is a series of photographs, and I would request the help of my learned colleague. I would like to be able to see photograph 12. Which page do I need to display in order to see this photograph? My case manager has found it, so let's see. Could we possibly enlarge photograph 12, please. I'm turning to the court officer now: Can we enlarge this, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is photograph 11.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is number 11, but I would need the number 12.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you describe to me what one can see on this photograph, please, and from which side in relation to the crater formed by the explosion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are looking from the direction of the crater, i.e., from the point where the explosive device landed. There's a concrete wall in the background of the photograph, and there are visible -- there's visible damage caused by shrapnel; and in the -- on the house behind, one can see that the whole roof had been blown away.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see the tires that are on the forefront here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can see tires scattered around. In the right-hand corner, one can see trees that were cut off by shrapnel and damaged to the tree branches. Also, the earth had been turned over and blown towards the wall.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could these tires mean that were there some military facilities close by?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That used to be a workshop, a car repair workshop and tire repair workshop. More precisely, Safeta Zajke is a street, a residential area, where there are only family houses. They're lined next to each other and all these houses were demolished.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree then that opposite this location, where the tires are, we found ourselves at the foot of Mount Zuc?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, behind the houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: At the time, did you know that the ABiH units were positioned on this mount?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I knew that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And on the 24th of June, 1995, did you and your team look into the question of any military activity or fire that could have come from Mount Zuc and that could have been the cause of this damage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The reason being that the damage is so extensive. It's much more extensive than the one caused by a mortar shell or a tank shell or a shell fired from a gun.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: But, Witness, if someone was firing from a tank or firing several shells, would the damage have been huge or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not even closely to the one caused by a modified air bomb. It caused devastation at the place where these bombs hit, but also within the radius around it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And what do you base this on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I base it on the fact that I have seen hundreds of mortar shells landing; and when a mortar shell lands on a concrete surface, you can see exactly the so-called rose. This is what we call it in criminal investigation parlance, the place where a mortar shell lands. And one can see also see the angle of firing. You can see the tail of the mortar shell as well, and the largest shells were those of 120-millimetre.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that on this photograph we mainly see the soil. We don't see tarmac. We see soil that has been overturned.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my previous answer, I said that both of soil was overturned, and one can also see fresh holes in the concrete wall. You can see these tires scattered around, you can see the damage on the trees to the right of the photograph, and you can see that there's a roof missing.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to continue talking about this incident. We mentioned the report which is exhibit number 560. This is a 65 ter document number 17 -- 56, page 2 to 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, Your Honour, I would have liked to make a comment as regards the translation of this document, because the first -- I would like to talk about the fourth paragraph of this first page, which does not reflect what has been said in B/C/S, and I would like to spell this out. This is the last paragraph on this page. In the text in English, which you have, and which is the only one you can use, it says: "[In English] stretches towards the south-east." [Interpretation] Whereas, I will ask the witness to read this part so that the interpreters can translate it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you start reading from --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: This is the last paragraph, the second sentence in the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well. "The projectile landed on the asphalt carriage way of Safeta Zajke Street in front of the house number 43. The crater made by the projectile is turned length-wise towards south, more precisely to the area of Lukavica, where the aggressor's firing positions are."

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would have liked to draw your attention to the fact that you are solely working with the English text. I believe this is very important. In the original text, it says "south."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Well, we have heard that, and we see that the mistake has been corrected.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like to continue with this report.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: This report deals with two events, doesn't it -- incidents, rather?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only see the first one.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Let's turn to the second page, please. I would like you to look at the text where it says, this is the last paragraph, "lice mjesta." Do you have it in front of you now? Does this have to do with a second incident in Majdanska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Majdanska Street. Yes. This last paragraph says that the point of the impact of the second projectile is on Majdanska Street, no number, next to the Novi Grad transformer station.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Now, as far as the crater is concerned, it faces south, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And the report says that the crater mentioned in the first incident is also addressed in this report. This is the incident that took place in Safeta Zajke Street.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But if I may add one thing, the previous incident on Safeta Zajke Street, there are photographs --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. Mr. Sachdeva is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, it's just for your benefit, but the translation corresponding to the paragraph counsel is talking about is the next page in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. This is in -- this is in paragraph 3.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I finish?

utterances.speaker: MR. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is on page 3 for the Bench. This is the same as the original. The original text and the translation tally.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I think you wanted to add something, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well. What I wanted to add was that at the place of impact of the projectile on Safeta Zajke Street, there's a photograph that I made which shows fragments of the modified air bomb rocket engines embedded in the asphalt and also the angle at which they are embedded. It shows that the direction is from the south; in other words, there's a photograph showing this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So you are saying that one can see on the photograph that it's towards the south, as is mentioned in this report.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. South or south-east.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you say it faces south, south-west [as interpreted]. There is quite a big difference between the two, particularly in the light of distances?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: At least on the transcript, Mr. President the witness answered: "Yes. South or south-east," and counsel is -- if she is referring to the previous answer, she said "south, south-west," just for that to be clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Did you mean to say south or south-east?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I said south-east. No matter. This was a mere rhetorical question; south-east, south-west, whatever the direction might be.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: This can, of course, have great bearing on the findings you make, can't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have to tell you one thing. My personal opinion, and I'm not a ballistics expert, since the aggressor forces were deployed all around Sarajevo. Sarajevo is in a depression. It's surrounded by hills. They were able to fire where they wanted, when they wanted. They had ample opportunity.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Now let's stick to this report. According to you, was this report drafted on the basis of reports that had been filed by each member of the investigation team?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like my case manager to bring up document 76, which is a 65 ter document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva, are you going to re-examine this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: For how long? And bear in mind the reputation that you have unfortunately developed for underestimating, which has been referred to your learned colleague for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, five to eight manipulates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Five to eight minutes. I have three to four questions, at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Isailovic, you have used the half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can see that, Your Honour. I think it's important for the Bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Another five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's very difficult with all these technicalities. We have document 76, 65 ter document, up on the screen I believe that my learned colleague did not ask for this document to be tendered.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can I ask you to turn to the last sentence of this report, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Will I read it?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Projectile came from the area of Pavlovac, south-east".

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that these were the findings that you made on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was in the report. Since there is a hill behind the site, we got information from reconnaissance teams that the projectiles came from that place.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: But you don't mention this in your report, Witness, neither you nor Mr. Kucanin Mirsad, who was the person who drafted the previous report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But there's another fact that is relevant to this incident; namely, the place where the projectile landed is cylindrical in shape and very long, and you don't need expert knowledge to establish from which direction the projectile came.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, if it was that easy in two reports which have been included in the investigation, you mentioned two opposite directions of fire, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: South, south-east.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that a while ago the report signed by Kucanin Mirsad, which we discussed together, we made changes to the translation and we established that the origin of fire was the south. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's what he wrote.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And, in this instance, we can see that is says south-east; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that each member of your investigation team drew up these conclusions with a view to drafting a final report which would recap everything concerning this incident. Is that why there were so many forensic technicians on the site?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva. Yes, just a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, to be precise, in the witness's report, in the English translation, and I understand also in the B/C/S version, it actually is written the projectile was fired from the Pavlovac area in the south-east; in other words, south-east refers to the location ever Pavlovac. Perhaps counsel can ask the witness where Pavlovac is on the map. I think that should be noted, in my submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I had something else in mind, and I'm not interested to know where Pavlovac is located. What I would like to establish with my cross-examination is this: There are blatant discrepancy between two reports prepared by the same investigation team, so this is the purpose of my questions. We know where Pavlovac is. We can all use a map. That is not so difficult. So I have concluded my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, can you just tell the Court that in your official job description were you responsible for determining the direction of fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was not responsible for determining the direction of fire, and I said as much at the beginning of my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And with respect to the incident on the 16th of June, 1995, were there persons from the bomb squad present when you did your investigation on the 26th of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Their presence was almost compulsory. It was indispensable in order to find any remaining mines or explosives that might be there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If we can just go to Exhibit P568, this is the document prepared by Mujo Music. This should be the first page. My apologies, excuse me. It's 567. I'm very sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, in the second paragraph that you see that, it says that members of the bomb squad were present, in that report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And in the next paragraph where it talks about the -- where it talks about the origin of fire, do you see that there, where it talks about the origin of fire from Lukavica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's written there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Does it say at all that it came from the west? Do you see that there at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And if we could go back to Exhibit 568.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness, this is your report. On the top right --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: -- on the top left-hand corner, do you see a date; and if you do, please tell the Court what date that is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: 26th of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: And was that the date that you conducted the investigation or that the investigation was conduct the for this incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-116 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That's the re-examination, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, that concludes your evidence. We thank you for giving it and you may leave. We are going to adjourn now and we will resume tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 19th day of April, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.45 p.m.,
